stories-3-49-jesus-fashions-clay-birds-h.title: Jesus Fashioning Live Birds from Clay in Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2
stories-3-49-jesus-fashions-clay-birds-h.note: Surah 3:49 presents Jesus declaring to the Sons of Israel that he will fashion the form of a bird from clay and breathe into it so that it becomes a living bird, matching the clay sparrows miracle in chapter 2 of the second-century Infancy Gospel of Thomas.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators state that the Quran preserves an authentic miracle from the childhood and ministry of Jesus that was left unrecorded in the four canonical Gospels.
discussion.reply: First-century New Testament writings contain no account of Jesus animating clay birds, and John 2:11 explicitly identifies turning water into wine at Cana as the first of His signs. The clay birds narrative first appears in the mid-second-century Greek Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2, alongside episodes of the child Jesus withering and striking down playmates.

stories-3-49-jesus-fashions-clay-birds-h.quranEn: And (He will make him) a messenger to the Sons of Israel. ‘Surely I have brought you a sign from your Lord: I shall create for you the form of a bird from clay. Then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird by the permission of God. And I shall heal the blind and the leper, and give the dead life by the permission of God. And I shall inform you of what you may eat, and what you may store up in your houses. Surely in that is a sign indeed for you, if you are believers.
quranHighlights: I shall create for you the form of a bird from clay. Then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird

sources.title: Infancy Gospel of Thomas
sources.en: And having made some soft clay, He fashioned out of it twelve sparrows. And it was the Sabbath when He did these things. And there were also many other children playing with Him. And a certain Jew, seeing what Jesus was doing, playing on the Sabbath , went off immediately, and said to his father Joseph: Behold, your son is at the stream, and has taken clay, and made of it twelve birds, and has profaned the Sabbath . And Joseph, coming to the place and seeing, cried out to Him, saying: Why do you do on the Sabbath what it is not lawful to do? And Jesus clapped His hands, and cried out to the sparrows, and said to them: Off you go! And the sparrows flew, and went off crying. And the Jews seeing this were amazed, and went away and reported to their chief men what they had seen Jesus doing.

stories-3-35-37-wife-of-imran-dedicates-.title: Wife of Imran Dedicating Mary to the Temple and Angels Bringing Her Food
stories-3-35-37-wife-of-imran-dedicates-.note: Surah 3:35–37 narrates the wife of Imran vowing her unborn child to the sanctuary, naming her Mary, and Zachariah finding miraculous food with her in the prayer chamber, matching Anna's vow and Mary's temple upbringing in Protevangelium of James 4 and 8.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes regard Mary's dedication to the Jerusalem sanctuary under the guardianship of the priest Zachariah and her miraculous out-of-season provisions as revealed prophetic biography.
discussion.reply: Under Mosaic law (Numbers 3:10; 18:1–7), residency and service inside the Temple sanctuary were restricted to male Levites and Aaronic priests, and canonical Gospels place Mary at home in Nazareth (Luke 1:26–28). The story of Mary's mother vowing her unborn child to the Temple and Mary living inside the sanctuary fed by an angel originates in the mid-second-century Greek Protevangelium of James 4:1 and 8:1.

stories-3-35-37-wife-of-imran-dedicates-.quranEn: [35] (Remember) when the wife of ‘Imrān said, ‘My Lord, surely I vow to You what is in my belly, (to be) dedicated (to Your service). Accept (it) from me. Surely You – You are the Hearing, the Knowing.’ [36] And when she had delivered her, she said, ‘My Lord, surely I have delivered her, a female’ – God knew very well what she had delivered, (since) the male is not like the female – ’and I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her with You, and for her descendants, from the accursed Satan.’ [37] So her Lord accepted her fully and caused her to grow up well, and Zachariah took charge of her. Whenever Zachariah entered upon her (in) the place of prayer, he found a provision (of food) with her. He said, ‘Mary! Where does this (food) come to you from?’ She said, ‘It is from God. Surely God provides for whomever He pleases without reckoning.’
quranHighlights: when the wife of ‘Imrān said, ‘My Lord, surely I vow to You what is in my belly, (to be) dedicated (to Your service).

practices-3-96-97-hajj-pilgrimage-to-bak.title: Pilgrimage (Hajj) to the House at Bakkah and the Station of Abraham
practices-3-96-97-hajj-pilgrimage-to-bak.note: Surah 3:96–97 mandates pilgrimage (Hajj) to the ancient sanctuary at Bakkah and its inviolable precinct, incorporating the pre-Islamic Meccan circumambulation rite attested in the sixth-century Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma.

discussion.view: Islamic tradition holds that Bakkah is an ancient name for Mecca where Abraham and Ishmael raised the first house of worship and left Abraham's footprint on the stone station (Maqam Ibrahim).
discussion.reply: Verse 17 of the pre-Islamic Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (~AD 590) swears by 'the sacred edifice around which the men of Quraysh and Jurhum, who built it, make devout processions,' attesting before Islam that the Meccan shrine was venerated by Arab tribes as an ancient house of circumambulation and sanctuary truce.

practices-3-96-97-hajj-pilgrimage-to-bak.quranEn: [96] Surely the first House laid down for the people was indeed that at Becca, a blessed (House) and a guidance for the worlds. [97] In it are clear signs: the standing place of Abraham. Whoever enters it is secure. Pilgrimage to the House is (an obligation) on the people to God – (for) anyone who is able (to make) a way to it. Whoever disbelieves – surely God is wealthy beyond the worlds.
quranHighlights: Surely the first House laid down for the people was indeed that at Becca
Whoever enters it is secure. Pilgrimage to the House is (an obligation) on the people to God

phrases-3-24-the-fire-will-touch-us-for-.title: People of the Book Saying: 'The Fire Will Touch Us for a Number of Days'
phrases-3-24-the-fire-will-touch-us-for-.note: Surah 3:24 quotes People of the Book saying 'The Fire will touch us for a number of days,' matching the rabbinic doctrine codified in Mishnah Eduyot 2:10 that 'the judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom continues twelve months.'

discussion.view: al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr note that Surah 3:24 quotes the claim of Medinan Jews who held that their punishment in the Fire would last for a fixed, limited duration.
discussion.reply: The verse accurately reflects the rabbinic tradition preserved in Mishnah Eduyot 2:10 (compiled c. AD 200), in which Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri define the judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom as lasting either twelve months or from Passover to Shavuot.

phrases-3-24-the-fire-will-touch-us-for-.quranEn: That is because they said, ‘The Fire will only touch us for a number of days.’ What they forged has deceived them in their religion.
quranHighlights: they said, ‘The Fire will only touch us for a number of days.’

sources.title: Mishnah Eduyot
sources.en: The judgment of the wicked in gehinom [continues] twelve months, for it is said, and “It will be from one month until its [same] month” (Isaiah 66:23). Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: “[As long as] from Passover to Shavuoth, for it is said, “And from one Sabbath until its [next] Sabbath” (ibid.).
highlights: The judgment of the wicked in gehinom [continues] twelve months
[As long as] from Passover to Shavuoth

stories-3-42-44-casting-pens-as-lots-for.title: Priests Casting Their Pens as Lots to Decide Who Will Guard Mary
stories-3-42-44-casting-pens-as-lots-for.note: Surah 3:42–44 cites as unseen knowledge how the temple priests disputed and cast their pens or rods (aqlamahum) as lots to determine who would become Mary's guardian, matching the lot-casting in the Protevangelium of James 8:2–9:1.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that the temple priests cast their reed pens into the Jordan River to settle their dispute over who would raise the child Mary after Zechariah claimed priority through his marriage to her maternal aunt.
discussion.reply: The canonical Gospels never place Mary's upbringing inside the Jerusalem Temple or mention a priestly lottery for her guardianship. That episode comes from the second-century Greek Protevangelium of James 8:2–9:1, where the high priest Zacharias summons the widowers to bring their rods to the Temple so a sign may designate who will take the virgin of the Lord into his keeping.

stories-3-42-44-casting-pens-as-lots-for.quranEn: [42] And (remember) when the angels said, ‘Mary! Surely God has chosen you and purified you, and He has chosen you over all other women. [43] Mary! Be obedient to your Lord, and prostrate yourself and bow with the ones who bow.’ [44] – That is one of the stories of the unseen. We inspired you (with) it. You were not with them when they cast their pens (as lots to see) which of them would take charge of Mary. Nor were you with them when they were disputing. –
quranHighlights: You were not with them when they cast their pens (as lots to see) which of them would take charge of Mary.
Nor were you with them when they were disputing.

sources.title: Protevangelium of James
sources.ref: Protevangelium of James 8:2-3 (Priests Summoning Widowers with Their Rods)
sources.en: And when she was twelve years old there was held a council of the priests , saying: Behold, Mary has reached the age of twelve years in the temple of the Lord. What then shall we do with her, lest perchance she defile the sanctuary of the Lord? And they said to the high priest : You stand by the altar of the Lord; go in, and pray concerning her; and whatever the Lord shall manifest unto you, that also will we do. And the high priest went in, taking the robe with the twelve bells into the holy of holies; and he prayed concerning her. And behold an angel of the Lord stood by him, saying unto him: Zacharias, Zacharias, go out and assemble the widowers of the people, and let them bring each his rod; and to whomsoever the Lord shall show a sign, his wife shall she be. And the heralds went out through all the circuit of Judæa, and the trumpet of the Lord sounded, and all ran.
highlights: Mary has reached the age of twelve years in the temple of the Lord.

sources.en: And Joseph, throwing away his axe, went out to meet them; and when they had assembled, they went away to the high priest , taking with them their rods. And he, taking the rods of all of them, entered into the temple, and prayed ; and having ended his prayer , he took the rods and came out, and gave them to them: but there was no sign in them, and Joseph took his rod last; and, behold, a dove came out of the rod, and flew upon Joseph's head. And the priest said to Joseph, You have been chosen by lot to take into your keeping the virgin of the Lord.
